title: MS2CAST: A Video Anomaly Detection Framework via Multi-Scale Spatial Cross-Attention and Efficient Spatiotemporal Networks
approach: Frame-prediction (semi-supervised): MViTv2-S + ConvNeXt-T multi-scale cross-attention encoder with SwinLSTM/VMRNN latent dynamics, no optical flow
protocol_notes: Frame-level AUC; micro/macro not stated. The anomaly-score coefficient w is tuned per dataset. For the selected Pre-LN + SwinLSTM model it is 0.6 on Ped2 (Table 3), 0.9 on Avenue (Table 4 and Sec. 4.6) and 0.2 on ShT (Sec. 4.5). Table 8 compares only against older frame-level methods (best ShT baseline is CF2M-Net at 73.9). Its claim of 'outperforming all of them on ShanghaiTech' therefore holds only against those chosen baselines, not against object-centric, pose or VLM methods.
hardware: single NVIDIA A100 40GB; selected Pre-LN cross-attention + SwinLSTM: 62 ms latency, 68 FPS, 806 MB peak GPU memory (Table 7)
supervision_evidence: Sec. 3.6: 'Our predictive model is trained exclusively on normal samples'. The paper calls itself a 'semi-supervised' (normal-only) framework. The ImageNet MViTv2-S/ConvNeXt-T backbones are frozen, and the cross-attention, SwinLSTM and decoder are trained separately per dataset (Sec. 4.2: Ped2 bs16/lr 2e-4/25 ep, Avenue bs32/5e-4/15 ep, ShT bs128/1e-3/5 ep).
lookahead_frames: 0-1 for the raw score. Eqs. 37-38 compute S(t) from the predicted frame I_{t+1}, using inputs I_{t-3:t}. The paper does not say whether S(t) is matched to the label of frame t or of frame t+1; the usual Liu et al. alignment to the predicted frame gives 0. The per-video min-max (Eqs. 39-40, 't′ ranges over all frame indices within a given video clip') uses the whole test video. The width and centring of the final '1D Gaussian filter' are not stated.
notes: CORRECTED: only the lookahead text changed. The earlier row said frame t+1 'is scored against its own ground truth'. In Sec. 3.6, 'ground truth' means the real frame I_{t+1}, not the label. S(t) is indexed t but computed from I_{t+1}, so whether the score is 0 or 1 frame ahead of its label is not stated. Supervision and all other flags are confirmed. Per-video min-max normalisation is applied separately to the PSNR and MS-SSIM scores. These are mixed with weight w and then smoothed by a '1D Gaussian filter' (sigma not given; causal or centred not stated). w is chosen per dataset from test-AUC sweeps (Sec. 4.6, Fig. 6): Ped2 0.6, Avenue 0.9 and ShT 0.2 for the selected Pre-LN + SwinLSTM model, and Avenue 1.0 for Post-LN in Sec. 4.3. The loss weight alpha was also tuned on Avenue/Ped2 test AUC (Table 2). ShT uses the standard 330/107 one-class split. AUC aggregation (micro/macro) is not stated. No optical flow.

title: MoG-VLM: Efficient Video Anomaly Detection through Motion-Guided Vision-Language Models
venue: BMVC 2026 (per arXiv comment 'Accepted at BMVC 2026'; proceedings not checked)
approach: Training-free zero-shot VLM/LLM pipeline: motion-guided adaptive frame selection, Qwen3-VL-8B captioning, VideoLLaMA3-7B temporal stream, Qwen3-4B scoring, tier-aware fusion
protocol_notes: The dataset section says ShanghaiTech 'contains 107 testing videos', which is the standard one-class test split. The method is training-free, so the training split does not matter. FPS is amortized (N_frames / T_pipeline), not per-frame latency. Table 1 mixes protocols: MULDE 86.70 (its object-centric number) sits next to 'Yu Wang et al.' 98.13 on ShT, which is most likely a weakly supervised split. MoG-VLM trails AnyAnomaly (79.70) among the zero-shot methods on ShT, and the paper itself only calls ShT 'competitive'.
hardware: single NVIDIA A100 40GB
supervision_evidence: Conclusion: 'a zero-shot training-free framework'. Sec. 2: the gating mechanism is 'entirely training-free'. It uses off-the-shelf Qwen3-VL-8B, VideoLLaMA3-7B and Qwen3-4B. The only adaptive statistics are online EMA z-scores of the motion (TGM) signal. There is no memory bank and no use of normal training videos.
lookahead_frames: Not stated as one number, but above 0. (i) An anchor at t_i triggers dense re-scoring of [t_i−5,t_i), [t_i−15,t_i−5) and [t_i−30,t_i−15) (Sec. 3.4.2/4.2) and upgrades their tier and λ. A frame's final score can therefore depend on a frame up to 30 frames later. (ii) The motion gate densifies sampling in [t−Δt, t+Δt] with Δt=1 s (Eq. 4), so the sampling of earlier frames depends on motion up to 1 s later. (iii) The temporal-stream window is centred on the target (Eq. 9, ±ω, ω not given). It is implemented as 10 frames from non-overlapping 64-frame windows whose score is 'propagated forward in time until the next window'. If that score applies from the window start, the lookahead is up to about 63 frames; this is not stated. (iv) Gaussians with σλ=0.25 s and σ=1.0 s have unstated centring.
notes: CORRECTED: only the lookahead text changed. The earlier row called the anchor lookback windows 'past-only'. They are past-only relative to the anchor, but they re-score the frames before it. A frame's score therefore depends on whether a frame up to 30 frames later became an anchor, and the motion gate reaches back Δt=1 s. Supervision and other flags are confirmed. Zero-shot: no target normal data is used. Two 1-D Gaussian filters are applied: σλ=0.25 s on λ_t, and σ=1.0 s on the fused score 'for evaluation stability'. Neither is stated to be causal. The z-score uses EMA running statistics of the motion signal, frozen when z>θ, not of the anomaly scores. θanom=2.3, λ=(0.3, 0.4, 0.7) and σ=1.0 are fixed 'across all datasets without per-dataset tuning'. However, App. A.1/A.4 justify λbase, λmotion and σ with sweeps on the test benchmarks, including ShT. ShT 'contains 107 testing videos' (the one-class test set). AUC micro/macro is not stated. FPS is amortised.

title: Efficient Zero-Shot Video Anomaly Detection via Signal-Aware Adaptive Fusion (SAAF)
venue: WACV 2027 (per arXiv comment 'Accepted at WACV 2027'; proceedings not yet available)
approach: Training-free zero-shot: CLIP ViT-B/32 delta/drift signals gate which frames go to Qwen3-VL-8B captioning and Qwen2.5-7B scoring, with conditional VideoLLaMA3-7B video-level fusion
protocol_notes: ShT split not stated. FPS is amortized throughput. Table 2 lists MULDE at 81.40 on Shang with no setting given. That matches neither of MULDE's own numbers (86.7 object-centric, 81.3 frame-centric micro). The sibling MoG-VLM paper lists MULDE at 86.70, so the baselines are inconsistent. AnomalyRuler (85.20) scores higher but is marked as not zero-shot. In an ablation, a rho-dominant weighting would add 0.93 points on ShT, but the default was kept 'to avoid dataset-specific' tuning.
hardware: single NVIDIA A100 40GB
supervision_evidence: Intro: adaptive EMA thresholding gives coverage of anomaly types 'without training data'. Table 2 marks SAAF as zero-shot and training-free. CLIP ViT-B/32 delta/drift signals, Qwen3-VL-8B, Qwen2.5-7B and VideoLLaMA3-7B are all used off the shelf. Thresholds come from online EMA running statistics (10-frame warm-up), not from normal training videos.
lookahead_frames: Not stated numerically. The VideoLLaMA3 clip is '10 frames centered at the anchor' (C_t = {f_{t−k},…,f_t,…,f_{t+k}}; k not given). That is about 5 frames ahead if the clip uses consecutive native frames, and up to about 80 if it uses the stride-16 sampled frames; the spacing is not stated. Anchor scores are forward-filled for up to M=64 frames, which is causal. The σ=100-frame Gaussian (≈3.3 s at 30 fps, 'Following [14]') has unstated centring; if centred, it reaches hundreds of frames ahead.
notes: CORRECTED: (1) The lookahead was 'about 5', which assumed consecutive clip frames. The clip-frame spacing is not stated, and the delta/drift signals run on stride-16 sampled frames. (2) The EMA thresholds are evidently initialised per video. 'A warmup period of 10 frames initializes the running statistics', and both the MSAD Robbery 1 failure case ('anomaly begins at frame 0, contaminating baseline statistics during warmup') and the Limitations assume a per-video warm-up. This is a causal per-video calibration of the frame selector, not a normalisation of the scores, so per_video_normalisation stays not_stated. Delta and drift use the previous sampled frame and the preceding W=20 sampled (stride-16) frames. Supervision is confirmed: zero-shot, no target normal data. Unselected frames get the default score s_d=0.3. N=1, s_d and τf=0.4 were 'fixed a priori', and (0.6, 0.4) is kept 'to avoid dataset-specific tuning', although a ρ-dominant weighting would add 0.93 on ShT. The App. A sweeps are run on the test benchmarks. The ShT split is not stated (it cites Luo et al. 2017 [17]). AUC micro/macro is not stated. FPS is amortised.

title: Real-Time Video Anomaly Detection Using YOLO Pose Estimation and CLIP-Based Semantic Scoring
approach: Training-free scoring: YOLOv11n-pose person crops scored by CLIP ViT-B/32 cosine similarity to 4 fixed text prompts, Gaussian smoothing, threshold
protocol_notes: On Avenue and ShT the AUROC equals the authors' multi-feature baseline, which is a reimplementation of Reiss & Hoshen with YOLO detection. The footnote says both share the same YOLO detector and evaluation and only the scoring differs. Threshold theta*=0.7 is chosen on a validation partition. Scores are smoothed with a 1D Gaussian (sigma=5, half-window 15), which is non-causal if centred. YOLO is fine-tuned on CU Indoor Anomaly and reused for Avenue and ShT. Its 'Attr-Based [6]' row (86.0 / 71.1) is far below AccI-VAD's self-reported 93.7 / 85.9.
hardware: NVIDIA Titan XP (used for YOLO fine-tuning; the system is 'designed for deployment on a single desktop-class GPU (NVIDIA Titan XP)'). The Table III throughput GPU is not explicitly named. Live deploym
supervision_evidence: The method as described is training-free: 'CLIP ViT-B/32 is used with pre-trained weights without fine-tuning'. The score is the max over persons of the max cosine similarity to 4 fixed prompts (Eqs. 2-3). However, the Table I footnote and Sec. V-A show that the Avenue/ShT AUROC (89.26/70.26) is identical to the authors' reimplementation of Reiss & Hoshen, which uses GMM/kNN density over pose, velocity and CLIP features. The paper's explanation is 'Both pipelines share the same YOLO detector, so Avenue and ShanghaiTech values are identical'. Only CU Indoor differs (84.13 vs 82.12). A shared detector cannot by itself give identical AUROC from two different scorers, so it cannot be determined which scorer produced the reported numbers.
lookahead_frames: 0 for the raw score (frame t only, Eqs. 2-3). Smoothing uses a Gaussian kernel with σ=5 and 'half-window w=15'. A half-window implies a two-sided ±15-frame kernel, which is up to 15 future frames if aligned to frame t. Causality is not stated.
notes: CORRECTED: supervision changed from training_free to unclear. The reported Avenue/ShT numbers cannot be attributed to the CLIP scorer (see evidence). If they actually come from the GMM/kNN baseline, they are one-class density scores on target features. Reiss & Hoshen fit their density on normal training data, and this paper does not say what its reimplementation is fitted on. Only if the method description is trusted is the row training_free with no target data, and uses_target_normal_training_data=false is kept on that basis. A second issue: YOLOv11n-pose was fine-tuned on CU Indoor as a two-class detector with Normal and Abnormal person categories (Table II: precision 0.95 vs 0.86), so it was trained with external anomaly labels. Eqs. 2-3 do not use that class output, and the paper only says the detector is 'supervised for person localization'. The same fine-tuned YOLO is reused for Avenue and ShT. Granularity is hybrid: object-centric person crops scored zero-shot by CLIP; keypoints do not enter the score. θ*=0.7 was swept 'on a validation partition to maximize the AUROC', but AUROC does not depend on θ. Padding δ=10 was chosen on CU Indoor. AUROC micro/macro is not stated. No Ped2 results.

title: Strictly Causal Streaming Video Anomaly Detection with a Theoretically-Grounded State-Space Core
venue: arXiv preprint (the HTML header lists 'Journal: Pattern Recognition Letters', but the text says further edge benchmarks are 'planned before submission'; no acceptance)
approach: Causal streaming state-space model (2 layers, state size N=128, learned event-boundary decay gate) on frozen ImageNet ResNet-18 features, one-step-ahead feature prediction error
protocol_notes: The method is framed as strictly causal, yet the paper says 'scores are min-max normalized per clip before thresholding/AUC computation'. That needs the whole clip and so is non-causal at evaluation. ShT is not evaluated; the paper lists it as remaining work. There are no comparison rows (VADMamba could not be run on non-CUDA hardware). The paper admits the accuracy trails non-causal baselines. In the ablation, turning the gate off gives 76.6 on Ped2, but 67.9 is the main reported configuration.
hardware: Apple M3 Pro (PyTorch MPS backend); 0.74 ms/frame Ped2 (1343.62 FPS), 0.77 ms/frame Avenue (1290.74 FPS)
supervision_evidence: Sec. 3.4: 'The model is trained self-supervised on normal-only training clips' by next-embedding prediction (Eq. 7). Sec. 3.2: the ImageNet ResNet-18 backbone is frozen, and 'only the temporal core below is optimized'. The score is the one-step-ahead prediction error ||ê_t − e_t||.
lookahead_frames: 0 for the model ('there is no operation in the model that looks ahead'; the score at t uses the prediction made from e_1..e_{t−1}). However, the per-clip min-max normalisation uses the whole test clip (test video).
notes: CONFIRMED. Quote: 'scores are min-max normalized per clip before thresholding/AUC computation, following standard VAD evaluation protocol'. Sec. 5.1 also cites 'the standard per-clip minmax score normalization protocol'. Clips here are the test videos (Ped2 12, Avenue 21). This contradicts the strict-causality framing at evaluation time. No score smoothing is described; the scoring is fully specified as prediction error plus per-clip min-max. The only per-dataset difference stated is the epoch count (40 Ped2 / 30 Avenue), and the configuration is called 'initial, untuned'. The authors also say they did not adopt the better ablation rows (gate-off gives 76.6 on Ped2). ShT is not evaluated. AUC micro/macro is not stated. Timing is on an Apple M3 Pro (MPS).

title: Reliability-Aware Prototype Calibration for Frozen Pose-Flow Video Anomaly Detection (RPC)
authors: Dong, Su, Dong, Jiao, Guo, Pan
approach: Post-hoc prototype calibration on frozen one-class pose normalizing-flow detectors (STG-NF, DA-Flow); no trainable parameters added
protocol_notes: Pose-based and human-only; inherits the base detectors' pose pipelines. Likelihood and prototype terms are standardised with statistics from normal training windows only. ShT hyperparameters are chosen on a training-only proxy validation set, since there is 'no official validation split in the one-class setting'. Seed variance is reported. The re-run STG-NF baseline (85.52) is below the published 85.9. No Avenue or Ped2.
hardware: not stated
supervision_evidence: Sec. 4.1: 'All detectors are trained in the one-class setting. Only normal skeleton windows are used to compute frozen detector statistics, fit prototype centers and diagonal variances, and estimate normalization constants.' The training set 'contains only normal skeleton windows'. The STG-NF/DA-Flow backbones are frozen, and no trainable parameters are added. The listed 85.89 is STG-NF+RPC (Table 3).
lookahead_frames: About seg_len/2 − 1 frames from window placement. STG-NF writes each window score at window start + seg_len/2, which is about 11 frames for its default 24-frame window; RPC does not state T. On top of that come the tails of the centred Gaussians (sigma 1 to 6 applied in sequence, effective σ≈9.5 frames). This is inherited from the STG-NF evaluation pipeline and is not described in the RPC paper.
notes: CORRECTED: non_causal_smoothing changed from not_stated to yes, per_video_normalisation from not_stated to no, and the lookahead was filled in. All three come from the inherited evaluation pipeline. The paper says 'The checkpoint, cached skeleton input, and evaluation pipeline are then kept fixed', and converts window scores to frame scores 'by the corresponding frozen backbone evaluation pipeline'. The official STG-NF scoring code (scoring_utils.py: get_clip_score, smooth_scores, score_dataset) does the following: it writes each window score at window start + seg_len/2; it takes the minimum log-likelihood over persons per frame; it runs scipy gaussian_filter1d (centred) per clip with sigma 1 to 6 applied in sequence; and it concatenates all clips into one micro AUROC, with no per-video normalisation. None of this is described in the RPC text itself. Supervision is confirmed. RPC's own normalisation (Eq. 8) standardises with training-set statistics; rank-percentile is used for visualisation only. K, α and γ are selected per dataset: on UBnormal from its official validation split, and on ShT from a proxy validation set. That proxy set holds out 20% of normal training skeleton windows plus corrupted normal variants and synthetic pseudo-anomalies. These are used only for hyperparameter selection, not for training. Human-only (HR variants also reported). Five-seed mean ± std reported.

title: Bounding-Box Trajectories Matter for Video Anomaly Detection (TrajVAD)
approach: Object-centric trajectory density: normalizing flow over multi-class bounding-box trajectories (TrajVAD-T) plus a reliability-gated pose branch (TrajVAD-P)
protocol_notes: Trained on normal data only. Micro-averaged AUROC: scores are concatenated across all test videos. Pipeline: YOLOX + OSNet re-ID + ByteTrack, Kalman-smoothed boxes, AlphaPose for -P. Coordinates are normalised by frame resolution, and ActNorm is initialised from the first training batch; the paper states no other test-time normalisation. Preprocessing dominates cost: about 104 ms/frame for detection and tracking, plus 31 ms/frame for pose in -P. TrajVAD-T totals 107.2 ms/segment. No Avenue or Ped2. The same authors' evaluation paper (arXiv 2608.21854, Table 4) shows TrajVAD-P ShT micro-AUROC falling from 88.59 to 61.92 after video-mean replacement, which sets within-video AUROC to 50%.
hardware: not in main text (speed-benchmark hardware is in the supplementary material, not read)
supervision_evidence: The normalizing flow models the trajectory distribution 'through a likelihood-based objective trained solely on normal data'. ShT 'contains 330 normal training videos and 107 test videos'. 'All features are standardized using training-split statistics.' The NF (plus a pose NF for -P) is fitted on the training trajectories.
lookahead_frames: not_stated. Scores come from overlapping T-frame segments (T=16 on ShT, 12 on UBnormal, 24 on MSAD), with stride 1 in the cost analysis. The segment-to-frame assignment is not described. Gap filling by linear interpolation (≤10 frames) uses later detections.
notes: CONFIRMED. Bounding-box trajectory NF (TrajVAD-T) plus a reliability-gated pose branch (TrajVAD-P). The listed 88.6 is the -P variant. Sec. 4.2: 'We assign an anomaly score to each frame in the test set, concatenate scores across all test videos ... This micro-averaged protocol follows prior work [5, 16]'. That citation covers only AUROC aggregation; the paper does not say it reuses STG-NF's smoothing code. No per-video score normalisation is described, only training-split standardisation and per-segment NLL normalisation (Eq. 8). No frame-score smoothing is described. Boxes are 'smoothed with a Kalman filter' before windowing, and the paper does not say whether this is forward-only or an offline (RTS) smoother. Segment length T differs per dataset. K=6/18 is fixed across datasets but was chosen from depth sweeps run on the ShT/MSAD test sets (Fig. 4: 'Based on these results'). The pose weight λ is not reported in the main text. Also evaluates UBnormal and MSAD. No Ped2 or Avenue.

title: Geometry-Aware Semantic Reasoning for Training Free Video Anomaly Detection (MM-VAD)
authors: Zia, Ali, Ramzan, Abid, Rehman, Xiang
approach: Training-free LAVAD-style pipeline: VLRM captioning, hyperbolic audio-visual caption fusion, LLaMA-3B scoring, ImageBind cross-modal refinement
protocol_notes: Probably not comparable with one-class numbers. ShT 96.95 (and LAVAD 94.55) are far above any one-class result, which suggests a different split (likely the weakly supervised reorganisation) or protocol; the split is not stated. The only comparison is against LAVAD. The reported 26.5 GB VRAM exceeds the memory of a standard RTX 4080 (16 GB), an internal inconsistency the paper does not explain. At 1.69 s/frame (about 0.6 FPS) it is far from real time.
hardware: single NVIDIA RTX 4080 ('All experiments are conducted on a single NVIDIA GPU RTX 4080'); 26.5 GB VRAM reported; 27.0 s per 16-frame batch (1.69 s/frame)
supervision_evidence: Sec. 3.4: 'Given a video with N temporal segments, we initialise Q0 and refine it over K lightweight iterations'. The update is 'Qk+1 = Qk − η∇Qk Ltotal' on an unsupervised entropy + sparsity loss summed over that test video's segments (Eq. 7), 'yielding a video-specific, self-consistent prompt Q*'. All encoders and the LLM are frozen, but a continuous prompt is gradient-optimised on each unlabelled test video of the target dataset, and those videos contain anomalies.
lookahead_frames: The whole test video. Caption cleaning searches 'the entire set' of the video's segment captions (Eq. 3). Prompt Q is optimised per video with a loss over all N segments. The Mahalanobis refinement uses 'the video's global visual feature distribution' (Eq. 8).
notes: CORRECTED: supervision changed from training_free to unsupervised_unlabelled_mixed, and per_video_normalisation from not_stated to yes. This table's training_free class excludes gradient training on the target dataset. MM-VAD runs gradient descent on a continuous prompt for each test video, which is transductive test-time adaptation on unlabelled test data containing anomalies. The paper calls this 'lightweight test-time adaptation rather than training' and labels itself training-free/zero-shot like LAVAD. If the table keeps self-reported labels, it should at least be flagged as 'training-free + per-test-video TTA' and not pooled with pure zero-shot methods. per_video_normalisation=yes because two steps calibrate scores per video using whole-video statistics, though neither is min-max. The sparsity term λ|Σa_t − μ| pulls every test video's total anomaly mass toward the same prior μ, and the refinement weights neighbours by Mahalanobis distance to the video's own feature mean and covariance. uses_target_normal_training_data stays false (no normal training videos are used). Score refinement averages over the K nearest textual neighbours (Eq. 9); whether these come from the same video is not stated, and there is no temporal window. Hyperparameters are in supplementary App. C, which was not available. For ShT the paper cites Liu et al. 2018 [26]; the split is not stated and Zhong et al. is not referenced. Its LAVAD baselines (ShT 94.55, Ped2 96.11) have no stated source; to my knowledge the original LAVAD paper reports only UCF-Crime and XD-Violence. ShT 96.95 is far above one-class results, which suggests a different split or protocol, but this is unconfirmed. AUC micro/macro is not stated. About 1.69 s/frame; 26.5 GB VRAM reported on an RTX 4080.

title: Unified Video Anomaly Detection Model for Detecting Different Anomaly Types (UniVAD)
approach: One-class three-stream AE (skeleton, local-visual object, global-visual frame) with past-present-future feature prediction
protocol_notes: Micro and macro AUC both reported. † marks per-dataset tuning of the stream weights alpha, beta, gamma. Pipeline: YOLOv5 + ByteTrack + AlphaPose. It is the highest one-class ShT micro in this list but has no Avenue or Ped2 results. arXiv 2608.21854 (Table 4) shows UniVAD ShT micro falling from 89.32 to 61.30 after video-mean replacement.
hardware: not stated
supervision_evidence: Sec. 4.1: 'Based on the OCC setting, only normal data were used for training, whereas both normal and abnormal data were used for testing'. Sec. 2: 'In this study, the OCC mode was adopted.' Three AE streams are trained with the past-present-future feature prediction (FFPP) task, 200 epochs on each dataset.
lookahead_frames: not_stated. Each clip has T frames, with past at t=1, present at t=T/2 and future at t=T. T=8 for the visual streams and T=24 for the skeleton stream on ShT. How the clip score maps to a frame is not stated; if it goes to the present frame, that is about 4 (visual) or 12 (skeleton) future frames. A 1-D Gaussian filter is applied on top.
notes: CONFIRMED. Three streams: skeleton (AlphaPose), local-visual object (CLIP ViT-B/32 features of YOLOv5+ByteTrack tracks) and global-visual frame. The highest object score is assigned to the frame, and the stream scores are summed with weights α, β, γ (Eq. 15). 'Following [39] (Jigsaw-VAD), we apply a temporal one-dimensional Gaussian filter'; sigma and centring are not stated. Table 1, ShT micro/macro: 'Ours' with fixed weights (1.0, 0.1, 0.1) gives 89.3/91.5. 'Ours†' with α, β, γ tuned per dataset gives 89.5/91.6, using (1.0, 0.1, 0.01) for ShT. The listed 89.3 is therefore the fixed-weight row. The skeleton window T is still set per dataset (24 for ShT/NWPU, 16 for UB). Micro- and macro-AUC are both reported and defined. Also evaluates UBnormal and NWPU. No Ped2 or Avenue.

title: AnyAnomaly: Zero-Shot Customizable Video Anomaly Detection with LVLM
authors: Ahn, Jo, Lee, Kwon, Hong, Park
approach: Training-free LVLM (MiniCPM-V 8B) context-aware VQA over segments, CLIP key-frame selection, user text defines the anomaly
protocol_notes: Micro AUROC; zero-shot, with no training on the target data. Appendix B.2: the score-weighting hyperparameters gamma1-gamma3 are tuned for each VAD dataset (tuning adds 0.2-2.9 points). The 1.36 FPS comes from Table S4, measured on the C-ShT/C-Ave benchmarks, not the Table 5 setting. Table 5's AccI-VAD row (76.2 / 66.8 / 60.3) matches exactly MULDE's frame-centric AccI-VAD-GMM reimplementation, not AccI-VAD's own 85.9 ShT.
hardware: single NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090
supervision_evidence: arXiv 2503.04504, Sec. 3.4: 'Instead of tuning the LVLM, we propose a new prompt and context... to enable training-free zero-shot anomaly detection'. MiniCPM-V 8B and CLIP ViT-B/32 are used off the shelf (App. A.2); no target-data fitting.
lookahead_frames: Up to 23 + 4*sigma. Every frame of a segment gets the segment's score (official default clip_length=24, also the best length in Table S2), so the first frame of a segment uses 23 future frames. A centred scipy gaussian_filter1d (radius 4*sigma) follows. The paper does not give sigma; the official code grid-searches sigma in [1,29] (fixed default 15, about 60 frames).
notes: CORRECTED: per_video_normalisation changed from not_stated to no, and lookahead and tuning made concrete, from the official code (github SkiddieAhn/Paper-AnyAnomaly: functions/eval_func.py, vad_proposed_MiniCPM.py). The scores of all test videos are concatenated and smoothed with gaussian_filter1d. The filter is centred and also runs across video boundaries. They are then min-max normalised once over the whole dataset, which is global and not per video. With the default grid_search=True, the code picks sigma and the three weights by the best AUC on the test labels. The Table S3 'w/ tuning' rows (Ave 0.6/0.3/0.1 gives 87.3; ShT 0.5/0.3/0.2 gives 79.7) are exactly the Table 5 numbers, so gamma1-gamma3 were in effect tuned on the test set. The released scripts target C-ShT/C-Ave; Table 5 presumably uses the same evaluation function. Extra caveat for comparisons: in Table 5 'each anomaly class in the dataset was treated as X', and the maximum over classes is taken per segment (code: max over keyword_list). The target test set's anomaly category names are therefore given as prompts, which is prior knowledge of the test anomaly taxonomy. Zero-shot: no target normal training videos and no memory bank. The 1.36 FPS was measured on C-ShT/C-Ave.

title: No Need For Real Anomaly: MLLM Empowered Zero-Shot Video Anomaly Detection (LAVIDA)
approach: MLLM (LISA-style <SEG> token) with token compression, trained on pseudo-anomalies synthesised from external segmentation datasets; zero-shot on VAD data
protocol_notes: Not strictly one-class: trained on external data with synthetic anomalies and no VAD data. ShT split not stated explicitly; it is compared against AnomalyRuler's one-class numbers. Ped2 is reported only at pixel level (87.68). No Avenue.
hardware: not stated in main text
supervision_evidence: Sec. 4: 'Our training dataset includes a diverse collection of segmentation datasets without any VAD datasets'. Sec. 3.3 and Eq. 2: the Anomaly Exposure Sampler labels each segmentation sample as anomalous with probability p (frame labels 1_T) using its genuine category. Supp. B.1 (CVF open access): ADE20K, Mapillary, CityScape, refCOCO*, YouTube-VOS, Ref-YouTube-VOS, MeViS, Ref-DAVIS-17. Supp. B.2: Qwen2-VL-7B with LoRA plus the SAM2 decoder, trained end-to-end.
lookahead_frames: Up to 14. The official config for ShT uses total_sampled_frames=8 and sample_interval=2, i.e. 16-frame non-overlapping clips. One MLLM semantic feature per clip conditions every frame's score. The paper and supplement only say '8 frames' per clip.
notes: CORRECTED: the supplement does exist (CVF open-access CVPR 2026 supplemental); the earlier note said it was missing. The official code (github VitaminCreed/LAVIDA) resolves several flags. (1) ShT split: the loader uses testing/frames plus test_pixel_mask, the standard 107-video one-class test set, so 85.28 is not from the weakly supervised split. (2) No smoothing and no normalisation: validate() pools raw object-score logits and computes micro AUC, and also a per-video average; gaussian_filter1d is imported but never used. (3) Per-dataset settings: sample_interval differs (UBnormal 4, ShT 2, Ped2 1, UCF/XD 128 in the config; the supplement says 32 for UCF/XD). (4) train_acc.py uses the single configured target test set as its validation set and saves the checkpoint with the best test frame AUC each epoch, i.e. checkpoint selection on target test labels, if this script produced the paper's numbers. (5) The test-time prompt 'Anomaly types may contain {c}' is filled with the target dataset's anomaly categories (code ANOMALY_CLASS for ShT: bicycle, fight, throw, run, skate, etc.; 18 names), which is prior knowledge of the test anomaly taxonomy. One global setting (max K_E=30, p=0.5, 48 queries, 5 projector layers, compression ratio 0.2) was chosen from ablations that are all reported on the test benchmarks. Ped2 is pixel-level only; there is no Avenue result.

title: Leveraging Multimodal LLM Descriptions of Activity for Explainable Semi-Supervised Video Anomaly Detection (MLLM-EVAD)
venue: TMLR 2026 (TMLR bib at jmlr.org/tmlr/papers/bib/dfc2HpDSlH.bib; OpenReview id dfc2HpDSlH)
approach: Interpretable exemplar-based: MLLM (GPT-4o / Gemma 3) text descriptions of object-pair activity, Sentence-BERT embeddings, nearest-exemplar scoring, combined with T-EVAL
protocol_notes: Single-scene, trained on nominal videos only. GPT-4o is used for Avenue. Detectron2 + ByteTrack. Appendix E studies temporal Gaussian smoothing. The authors say their frame-level numbers are 'slightly-below SOTA' and argue frame AUC ignores spatial localisation. Datasets are ComplexVAD, Street Scene and Avenue; no Ped2 or ShT.
hardware: cluster of eight 80 GB NVIDIA A100 (one sufficient); Gemma 3 0.58 s ± 0.16 per query on a single A100
supervision_evidence: arXiv 2510.14896v2 (TMLR 02/2026), Sec. 3: exemplar sets are built 'by applying an exemplar selection algorithm to all of the sentence embeddings found in nominal training video'. Eq. 2: score = 1 - max cos(I_r, e). Only pretrained GPT-4o/Gemma 3, Sentence-BERT, Detectron2 and ByteTrack are used. The T-EVAL component also uses 'an exemplar selection algorithm that does not require any deep network training'; its AppearanceNet was trained on external MS-COCO, VOC2012 and annotated surveillance patches, not on the target data.
lookahead_frames: About 30 (about 1 s). Each description pairs frame t with F_{t+Delta} ('e.g., Delta = 30', 'approximately one second'), and ByteTrack tracks objects for 30 frames. T-EVAL tracklets add T-1=9 future frames (T=10). Delta is not stated specifically for Avenue.
notes: CORRECTED (minor): lookahead narrowed from '10-30' to about 30, because the MLLM pair (t, t+Delta) dominates and the T-EVAL tracklet adds only 9. Everything else is CONFIRMED. The method uses target normal videos as an exemplar memory bank and does no gradient training on the target. It is object-centric (object pairs and singles) plus MLLM text, so hybrid. 'All quantitative results reported in Tables 2, 4, and 3 are computed using raw, unsmoothed anomaly scores'; Gaussian smoothing appears only in Appendix E (ComplexVAD). The object-to-frame aggregation is not described, and the MLLM is used 'at sparse temporal intervals' with no interval given. th=0.65 is a single exemplar threshold; pair distance h has no value; GPT-4o is used for Avenue and Gemma 3 for ComplexVAD. T-EVAL's own thresholds were tuned on Ped1/Ped2. The authors could not reproduce T-EVAL's Avenue numbers ('most likely due to different parameters'). Avenue 88.4 is T-EVAL+MLLM-EVAD frame AUC (Table 4); micro/macro is not stated. There is no Ped2 or ShT result.

title: Video Anomaly Detection with Contours - A Study
approach: Object-centric interpretable: SAM contours of tracked objects in polar form, reconstruction/classification with VAE/LAE/TAE/RNN
protocol_notes: BoT-SORT with YOLOv7 (MS-COCO) for tracking and SAM ViT-H for masks. Contours are 'normalized on video-level with respect to the largest object of the same class encountered in the given scene' (input-feature normalisation, non-causal). A Gaussian filter is applied along time. Micro/macro not stated. This is an unfavourable result, well below SOTA.
hardware: not stated
supervision_evidence: Abstract: 'we investigate the potential of learning recurrent motion patterns of normal human behavior using 2D contours'. Sec. 3.3-3.4 and 4.1: VAE/LAE/TAE/R-RNN/C-RNN (and a One-Class SVM 'trained in an unsupervised fashion' on training contours) are trained on the standard training splits (16 Avenue training videos; ShT 274,515 training frames), which contain only normal videos.
lookahead_frames: Whole video at the input level: polar contours are 'normalized on video-level with respect to the largest object of the same class encountered in the given scene'. The reported TAE reconstructs track descriptors in tabular form. A temporal Gaussian filter (sigma not stated) is applied on top.
notes: CORRECTED: granularity changed from object_centric to pose_based. The authors frame the work as Pose-based VAD with human contours instead of skeletons ('this novel perspective on Pose-based Video Anomaly Detection'). Only human contours are extracted, and the paper is compared with PAD methods and the HR-Avenue/HR-ShT subsets. Note that it is a silhouette, not keypoints. Also corrected: the Avenue 87.14 and ShT 67.81 numbers both come from the same TAE model (Table 2), not the C-RNN. The '30 clusters + 8 neurons best across all benchmark datasets' setting belongs to the C-RNN. The TAE uses one setting (batch 16, MSE, 50 epochs, Adam 2e-4), 'selected by exploring the parameter space and selecting the ones that provide the best results'; the selection data is not stated. per_video_normalisation=yes refers to input-feature normalisation, which mixes 'video-level' and 'scene'; score-level normalisation is not described. Smoothing follows Georgescu et al. (2021b) 'across the temporal axis'; it is counted as non-causal because a centred kernel is assumed. The object/track-to-frame aggregation is not described, and micro/macro is not stated. Pipeline: YOLOv7 + BoT-SORT tracking and SAM ViT-H masks. Results are well below SOTA.

title: VADMamba: Exploring State Space Models for Fast Video Anomaly Detection
authors: Lyu, Zhao, Hu, Huang, Chen, Du
approach: Frame-centric Mamba: VQ-Mamba U-Net (NVSS blocks) for frame prediction + optical-flow reconstruction hybrid with clip-level fusion
protocol_notes: Scores are min-max normalised over t (Eq. 8), which is per video and non-causal, plus Gaussian smoothing. FPS includes data processing and scoring but not FlowNet 2.0 flow extraction as stated, and the GPU is not named. 256x256 input. Model size differs per dataset.
hardware: not stated
supervision_evidence: Sec. I: OCC is 'learning normal samples only in the training phase'. The FP (VQ-Mamba U-Net, t=16 input frames) and FR (flow reconstruction from FlowNet 2.0) networks are trained on the training videos (AdamW, lr 2e-4, Sec. III-A).
lookahead_frames: Whole test video: per-video min-max over all t (Eq. 8; code normalize_score_list_gel, 'normalize in each video') plus a centred Gaussian (code: cv2.GaussianBlur with ksize (5,0) and sigma 10, per video). The raw prediction score itself uses only the 16 past frames.
notes: CONFIRMED, now backed by the official code (github jLooo/VADMamba Evaluate_frame_flow.py and utils.py): per-video min-max and a centred Gaussian blur with sigma=10. Serious caveat: the clip-level fusion (Eq. 9) is oracle selection. In the code, each 'clip' is a whole test video. For each test video, the code computes the AUC of S_p and of S_r against the test ground truth and keeps the better one (NaN fallback for all-normal videos). The hybrid numbers are therefore optimistic. The NVSS block counts differ per dataset ({1,1,1,1} for Ped2/SHT, {2,2,2,2} for Avenue). FR is trained on 'the best-performing FP model', with an unstated selection criterion. The 90 FPS for the hybrid model on Ped2 'includes data processing and anomaly score calculation' but not FlowNet 2.0 flow extraction; the GPU is not named.

title: Video Anomaly Detection with Motion and Appearance Guided Patch Diffusion Model (MA-PDM)
approach: Diffusion: patch-based conditional diffusion predicting future frames with motion (temporal difference) and appearance conditions plus patch memory
protocol_notes: Frame-level AUC. The Table 1 caption says 'average AUC score' without defining it (micro/macro or run-average unclear); normalisation not described. The 45 FPS comes from the TD-vs-optical-flow ablation (Table 5), but that TD row's Ped2/Avenue AUCs equal the final model's. The GPU is not named. The authors list real-time inference speed as a weakness.
hardware: not stated (HUST HPC platform acknowledged)
supervision_evidence: arXiv 2412.09026 Sec. 3: 'In the training phase, we solely use normal video data and leverage the preceding frames'. The abstract describes a diffusion model 'trained to recover normal patterns exclusively'. UBnormal uses the standard one-class split.
lookahead_frames: 0 in the described score. Frame 7 is predicted from the previous six frames, and Eq. 16 gives Score = MSE(I_{N+1}, pred) + alpha*MSE(I_1, recon), where I_1 is the first, past frame of the window. Post-processing is not described.
notes: CONFIRMED. A patch-based conditional diffusion model predicts the full future frame, so frame-centric. Eq. 16's alpha is a per-dataset scoring weight: 'The values for alpha are (0, 0.2, 0.3, 1) across four datasets'. Training epochs also differ (1000 Ped2 / 300 Avenue / 30 ShT / 40 UBnormal). Test-time sliding-window stride is 64, with 5 DDIM steps. Sampling is stochastic, and the Table 1 'average AUC' is undefined (micro/macro or a run average). The paper mentions no min-max or temporal smoothing, and no official code was found to check. The 45 FPS comes from the TD-vs-OF ablation (Table 5); the GPU is not named.

title: An Attribute-based Method for Video Anomaly Detection (AccI-VAD; v1 title 'Attribute-based Representations for Accurate and Interpretable Video Anomaly Detection')
approach: Object-centric density: velocity + pose attributes + CLIP deep residual, kNN density scoring (interpretable)
protocol_notes: Micro and macro both reported, but the Table 2 'Ours' row mixes configurations (Table 3 ablation). Ped2 99.1/99.9 is Deep+Velocity (no pose on Ped2). Avenue 93.7/96.3 uses all three features. ShT micro 85.9 is Pose+Velocity (whose macro is 88.8), while ShT macro 89.6 is all three (whose micro is 85.1). Detector: ResNet50 Mask R-CNN (COCO); FlowNet2 velocity; pose keypoints. Scores are calibrated with min-max on the normal training set (causal-friendly), but a temporal smoothing filter is applied. v1 (as cited in MULDE Table 1 and the TIP 2024 bi-directional paper) gives Avenue 93.3; v2/TMLR gives 93.7. Several later papers compare against MULDE's frame-centric reimplementation (ShT 76.2).
hardware: NVIDIA RTX 2080: about 80 ms/frame preprocessing (detection + optical flow), about 5 ms for features and scoring; 12 FPS with an average of 5 objects per frame (BA-AED 24 FPS, HF2 12 FPS on the same h
supervision_evidence: arXiv 2212.00789v2 (TMLR 01/2025) Sec. 4.4: the method 'does not require training'. Sec. 3.5: 'we fit a separate estimator for each feature'. kNN (k=1) is used for pose and CLIP deep features and a GMM for velocity, on normal training-set features from pretrained Mask R-CNN, FlowNet2, AlphaPose and CLIP ViT-B/16.
lookahead_frames: 12 frames (Ped2/Avenue, sigma=3) or 28 frames (ShT, sigma=7). This is the radius int(4*sigma+0.5) of scipy gaussian_filter1d (truncate=4), applied per test video in the official evaluate.py. The README says 'We usually use --sigma=3 for Ped2 and Avenue, and --sigma=7 for ShanghaiTech'. The flow frame pair is unspecified.
notes: CORRECTED (minor): calibration detail. In the official evaluate.py, velocity and pose are min-max scaled with the training min and the 99.9th-percentile max. The deep features use the plain training max; the percentile line is commented out. The calibration scores come from leave-one-video-out kNN on the training set (score_calibration.py). Everything else is CONFIRMED. It is a memory bank / density fit on target normal data with no gradient training. Calibration uses training statistics, so it is not per video. The paper only says 'temporal smoothing filter'; the code uses centred gaussian_filter1d per video. Per-dataset choices: no pose on Ped2 (velocity + deep only, B=1 vs B=8); GMM with 2 components on Ped2 in the code vs n=5 in the paper; detection thresholds 0.5/0.8/0.8; sigma 3 vs 7; the ShT code path sums velocity + pose only. The Table 2 'Ours' row mixes feature configurations per dataset and per metric. Micro ShT 85.9 is pose+velocity on the standard 107-video one-class test set, so it is not above 90.

title: STNMamba: Mamba-based Spatial-Temporal Normality Learning for Video Anomaly Detection
venue: arXiv preprint (venue not stated; no journal version found by search)
approach: Lightweight frame-prediction Mamba dual encoder (MS-VSSB spatial, CA-VSSB temporal) + spatial-temporal fusion + multi-level memory
protocol_notes: Scores are min-max normalised with g(·) (Eq. 18), and the paper does not state the scope (per video or global). The trade-off tau=0.8 is selected by AUC on Ped2/Avenue. Efficiency is evaluated on Ped2 only.
hardware: efficiency measured on Nvidia GTX TITAN XP (training on RTX 3090)
supervision_evidence: arXiv 2412.20084: a frame-prediction dual encoder (MS-VSSB on RGB frames I_{t-n:t}, CA-VSSB on RGB differences) with four memory banks that 'only store prototypes of normal patterns' is trained on the standard training videos (Sec. IV-A). The introduction notes such methods 'rely exclusively on normal videos during training'.
lookahead_frames: 0 for the raw scores (n=4 consecutive past frames predict the next frame; memory distance on the same queries). The scope of the min-max g(.) is not stated, so any lookahead it causes is unknown.
notes: CONFIRMED. Eq. 18: S = tau*(1-g(Sp)) + (1-tau)*sum_i g(Sd_i), where g(.) is min-max normalisation of unstated scope. The form mirrors MNAD's score, and MNAD's code normalises per video, so per-video scope is likely but unconfirmed; no official code was found. No temporal smoothing is mentioned. The metric is called 'frame-level average AUC', which is ambiguous between micro and macro. One global setting: tau=0.8, lambda1=0.1, lambda2=0.01, memory sizes 80/60/40/20, top-k 60%. tau and k were chosen from a sensitivity analysis by AUC on the Ped2/Avenue test sets. Efficiency (40 FPS) is measured on Ped2 with a GTX TITAN XP; training used an RTX 3090.

title: Advancing Video Anomaly Detection: A Bi-Directional Hybrid Framework for Enhanced Single- and Multi-Task Approaches
approach: Frame-centric bi-directional middle-frame prediction with convolutional transformer + LI-ConvLSTM hybrid
protocol_notes: Scores are min-max normalised, scope not stated. Bi-directional prediction uses context clips up to t+12, so about 12 frames of look-ahead latency. Strong for a frame-centric method on ShT.
hardware: single NVIDIA RTX A5000 (10.65 ms per 256x256 RGB frame; 10.37 ms / 96 FPS grayscale)
supervision_evidence: arXiv 2504.14753 Sec. IV-B: the framework is 'trained end-to-end as an OCC with no pre-training' on the default training sets. '10% of the total clips from the default training set' are the validation set, used for early stopping on validation loss.
lookahead_frames: 12. Inference uses the sequence t-n..t+n with n=4 at a sampling interval of 3 (context clips up to X_{t+12}) to predict the middle frame t. Any extra lookahead from the min-max scope is unknown.
notes: CONFIRMED. Middle-frame bi-directional prediction scores frame t with L(X_t, X^_t) (Eq. 17), 'subsequently normalized using min-max normalization [2], [22], ...'. The scope is not stated. The cited MNAD [2] and FastAno [22] normalise per video in their public code. The official repo (sgd95/ConvTTrans-ConvLSTM) has only training code, with no evaluation script to check. No temporal score smoothing is mentioned; the only Gaussian is the spatial SSIM/weighted-MAE window. One setting for all datasets: lambda=1, eta=0.75 ('sufficient but not optimal for any dataset', after an eta sweep on test AUC), and N=5 ConvTTrans blocks. Only the input channels differ (grayscale UCSD, RGB others). Frame AUC averaging (micro/macro) is not stated. Speed is 94 FPS RGB / 96 FPS grayscale on one RTX A5000.

title: Vision-Language Models Assisted Unsupervised Video Anomaly Detection (VLAVAD; arXiv PDFs titled 'Local Patterns Generalize Better for Novel Anomalies')
approach: VLM-assisted object-level: Selective-Prompt Adapter maps RPN object crops to semantic space, Sequence State Space Module (S3M) for temporal inconsistency
protocol_notes: Micro AUC on the standard ShT version (the paper uses the first version, 107 test videos). RPN object proposals, CLIP used to generate labels, Gaussian smoothing of the final score. The temporal part is trained only on normal training videos. The table cites AccI-VAD [76] for the metric but omits its and MULDE's numbers. The caption mentions UBnormal, but the table has no UBnormal column. Not peer-reviewed.
hardware: one NVIDIA A100
supervision_evidence: arXiv 2409.14109v2 PDF, Sec. 3.2: S3M 'undergoes unsupervised training solely on the normal samples within the training set'. Sec. 4.2: 'The temporal part of the framework only learns on the training videos without anomalies'. Sec. 4.1: 'The training sets of ShanghaiTech, Avenue and UCSD Ped2 contain only normal events' and 'As our approach is unsupervised, we use the first version' of ShT (the one-class split, 107 test videos).
lookahead_frames: not_stated (S3M predicts future features from past ones, but the final score gets 'Gaussian smoothing' of unstated width and alignment)
notes: CONFIRMED. Object-centric plus VLM: pre-trained YOLOX or an off-the-shelf RPN for proposals, ByteTrack tracks and 224x224 crops. The SPA static caption score is the max over objects in a frame, and the S3M temporal score is added. The spatial part is trained with CLIP-generated labels on the dataset's own training split, which is normal-only for Ped2, Avenue and ShT. Sec. 4.2 says the same spatial procedure is also used 'on the datasets where training data includes anomalies'. Added detail: during training the SPA picks one prompt per dataset from a prompt pool. That is per-dataset adaptation fitted on training data, not a reported hyperparameter sweep, so per_dataset_tuning stays not_stated. 'Non-causal' is inferred, because Gaussian smoothing is normally a centred filter; the paper gives no width. Micro-AUC. Table 1 is an image, so its numbers cannot be checked from the text layer. No per-video normalisation is mentioned. Not peer-reviewed.

title: VideoPatchCore: An Effective Method to Memorize Normality for Video Anomaly Detection
approach: Training-free memory bank (PatchCore-style) of CLIP local/global spatio-temporal patch features with coreset subsampling and kNN scoring
protocol_notes: Micro AUROC. YOLOv5 detector. Local and global scores are z-normalised (Eq. 12, mean/std; the source of the statistics is not stated) and fused with per-dataset weights (gamma 0.7/0.3 for Avenue, 0.9/0.1 for ShT). LAS weights delta are also per dataset. 1D Gaussian smoothing at test time. Per-dataset coreset ratio (1% / 25% / 10% for Avenue / SHTech / Corridor). No Ped2. SHTech speed ranges from 170.9 FPS (1%) to 31.0 FPS (99%).
hardware: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090
supervision_evidence: arXiv 2409.16225: uses CLIP's ResNet-101 vision encoder 'without additional training' plus a pretrained YOLOv5; 'our method requires no training'. Memory banks are built from normal training-video features with greedy coreset subsampling, and scoring is nearest-neighbour distance (Eq. 8-9).
lookahead_frames: Up to d-1 future frames: in the released code each non-overlapping d-frame clip gets one score, copied to all d frames (d=4 ShT, 10 Avenue; dataset.py steps by clip_length). On top of that comes a symmetric scipy gaussian_filter1d with sigma grid-searched over 0..19 on the test set, which reaches up to about ±76 frames at the default truncate=4.
notes: CONFIRMED. Released code (Memorization/inferencing.py, calc_best_auc): the global-stream score is z-scored per test video, and the local stream is z-scored over the concatenated test set. The Gaussian sigma and the fusion weights (a1/a2, b1/b2) are chosen by maximising test AUC, which is test-set tuning. The global Gaussian runs per video; the local one runs over scores concatenated across videos. The paper only gives the Eq. 12 z-normalisation (no source for the statistics), a '1D Gaussian filter during testing', and fixed per-dataset gamma (0.7/0.3 Avenue, 0.9/0.1 ShT) and delta (0.7/0.3 Avenue, 0.5/0.5 ShT). Per-dataset coreset ratio (1/25/10%), pooling channels (32/64) and input frames (10/4/4). Added detail from the released config: the kNN-distance exponent power_n differs per dataset (4 Avenue, 2 ShT, 1 IITB) and is not in the paper. Avenue object crops are also 64x64 in ObjectDetection/extra/config.py, while the paper says 224x224. Training-free, but the memory bank uses target normal data. Local YOLOv5 object stream plus global frame stream. Micro AUROC. No Ped2.

title: Follow the Rules: Reasoning for Video Anomaly Detection with Large Language Models (AnomalyRuler)
venue: ECCV 2024 (arXiv comment 'Accepted at European Conference on Computer Vision (ECCV) 2024')
approach: LLM rule-based reasoning: few-normal-shot rule induction (CogVLM-17B + GPT-4) and deduction (Mistral-7B); no training
protocol_notes: Few-shot: n=10 batches with m=1 normal reference frame each. Image-only input. Micro/macro not stated. Perception smoothing uses a majority vote with padding p=5 (uses neighbouring future frames) plus EMA (alpha=0.33). Relies on the proprietary GPT-4 API for induction; the paper says using GPTs on entire test sets is too costly.
hardware: not stated in text read
supervision_evidence: arXiv 2407.10299: 'Rule Generation module that uses a frozen LLM to generate rules', with no training or fine-tuning (Table 3 'Training' column unticked). 'The normal reference frames used by AnomalyRuler are randomly sampled from the normal training set'; n=10 batches x m=1 frame in the same-domain setting (Table 3).
lookahead_frames: Paper: 5 future frames (Eq. 1 majority vote over a centred window with padding p=5). On top of that, the threshold tau = mean of all EMA values of the video, which also sets the decay (1-tau) in the Eq. 2 score EMA, so whole-video statistics are used. Released code (majority_smooth.py): ema_majority_smooth is called with window_size=1, so the vote reduces to thresholding at tau with no future frames. Description modification looks at ±1 neighbouring frame. tau is still the per-video mean of the EMA, so the whole video is used. Final score: utils.evaluate_from_result applies a causal per-video EWM (span=10) to the LLM's 0/1 outputs.
notes: CORRECTED: lookahead and notes updated from the released code (github.com/Yuchen413/AnomalyRuler); the class and flags are unchanged. (1) The code's majority-vote window is 1, not p=5. Non-causal is still 'yes' because tau is the mean of the whole video's EMA, computed inside evaluate() for each video file. (2) The code computes AUC on concatenated scores and labels across videos, i.e. micro AUC; the paper does not state micro or macro. (3) The final score in code is an EWM with span 10 rather than Eq. 2's alpha=tau. (4) majority_smooth.main loads the ShT-derived anomaly keyword list (rule/rule_SHTech.npy) for every dataset. Unchanged: no network is fitted. Rules come from about 10 normal training frames of the target dataset (CogVLM-17B perception + GPT-4 induction); Mistral-7B does the deduction. Image-only and frame-level. 'Per-video normalisation' here means a per-video adaptive threshold (tau = mean of EMA values), not min-max scaling. One default hyperparameter set is used for all datasets, but p=5 is called 'the optimal window size for ShT' from the Fig. 3 test-set ablation. Relies on the proprietary GPT-4 API.

title: DA-Flow: Dual Attention Normalizing Flow for Skeleton-based Video Anomaly Detection
approach: Pose density: normalizing flow with a dual attention module after the GCN (STG-NF successor)
protocol_notes: Micro AUC. AlphaPose + YOLOX for skeleton tracking, a very large pose front-end compared with the tiny flow model. Human-only anomalies. Segment length differs per dataset (T=24 STC, 4 UB, 20 Ped2).
hardware: Intel i5-11400F + NVIDIA RTX 3080
supervision_evidence: arXiv 2406.02976v1 Sec. IV-A: 'our training process exclusively utilizes normal samples, with anomalous events introduced solely during the testing phase'. Anomalies are added to training only in the Sec. IV-E contamination robustness ablation (Fig. 9).
lookahead_frames: not_stated (each T-frame pose segment is scored; T=24 STC, 20 Ped2, 4 UB; the paper does not say which frame of the segment receives the score)
notes: CONFIRMED. Normalizing flow (K=8 steps, GCN + DAM) over AlphaPose + YOLOX skeleton tracks. Frame score = minimum log-likelihood over people (Eq. 1). Segment length T differs per dataset; added detail: T appears to be picked from the window-size sweep in Fig. 12, which reports the evaluation AUC ('optimal performance is achieved at T=24' for STC, T=4 for UB). No validation split is mentioned, so the selection is probably made on the test set. Other training hyperparameters are shared (Adam 5e-4, 8 epochs, batch 256). No score smoothing or normalisation is mentioned. Its predecessor STG-NF's released scorer applies per-clip Gaussian smoothing, but DA-Flow does not say whether it reuses that, and no code link is given. Human-only anomalies. Micro AUC. ShT 86.5 is the one-class split (330/107). Not peer-reviewed.

title: MULDE: Multiscale Log-Density Estimation via Denoising Score Matching for Video Anomaly Detection
approach: Density: multiscale log-density via denoising score matching + GMM over noise levels, on object-centric (AccI-VAD features) or frame-centric (Hiera) features
protocol_notes: Micro and macro. The object-centric pipeline follows Reiss & Hoshen (CLIP deep features, FlowNet 2.0 velocity, AlphaPose pose). Hiera-L frame-centric features take 130 ms per feature, and Hiera-base allows '25 FPS' on a 2080Ti. That is not the object-centric setting, so fps is left null. Frame-centric ShT is 81.3.
hardware: NVIDIA RTX 2080Ti
supervision_evidence: arXiv 2403.14497 Sec. 4: 'All our experiments were run in the one-class classification setting, that is, we used no anomalous videos for training.' The log-density MLP is trained by denoising score matching on normal-video features, and a GMM is fitted over noise scales on training data.
lookahead_frames: not_stated (1D Gaussian smoothing with unreported sigma; the temporal span of the FlowNet2 velocity features and the alignment of the 16-frame Hiera clips are not specified)
notes: CONFIRMED. The reported 99.7 / 94.3 / 86.7 are the object-centric 'MULDE (ours)' micro AUC in Table 1, using AccI-VAD features (CLIP deep, FlowNet2 velocity histograms, AlphaPose); the frame score is the max over objects. The frame-centric Hiera-L variant gives ShT 81.3. Features and per-feature scores are standardised with training-set statistics; no test-time or per-video normalisation is described. Supp.: 'these scores are temporally smoothed with a 1d-Gaussian filter', sigma not given. Added context: the public AccI-VAD evaluator that MULDE's features come from applies a per-video centred gaussian_filter1d with default sigma=3, but MULDE does not say it reuses it. Noise range [1e-3, 1] kept 'for all data sets' and 'we did not fine-tune these hyperparameters'. Beta=0.1 was taken 'as a compromise among performance on the three data sets' from the Table 3 frame-centric test results: a single value, but chosen on test data. The public repo is only a toy example.

title: Multi-Scale Video Anomaly Detection by Multi-Grained Spatio-Temporal Representation Learning
authors: Zhang, Wang, Qi, Sun, Zhuang, Ren, Ma, Liao
approach: Self-supervised proxy tasks (continuity judgment, discontinuity localization, contrastive missing-frame estimation) on frame or multi-task backbones
protocol_notes: The numeric fields give the best variant without virtual data. ∗ means it 'utilize[s] multi-task model ([11] or [12]) as backbone' (Georgescu et al. object-centric SSMTL/BA-AED); the Zhang paper itself does not name the detector. ▽ variants train on a virtual dataset with synthetic anomalies, so they are not strictly one-class. The plain version (92.4 / 85.1) is what most later papers cite. No Ped2. Micro and macro reported.
hardware: NVIDIA RTX 3090
supervision_evidence: CVPR 2024 paper: the three proxy tasks (continuity judgment, discontinuity localization, missing-frame estimation) follow the setting 'only learning from normal data'. The reported 93.6 / 86.8 are the micro AUCs of the 'Ours* (Three Tasks)' row in Table 3, which has no ▽ mark (▽ = 'apply virtual dataset for training'). The ▽ rows are Ours▽ = 93.2 / 86.2 and Ours▽* (Three Tasks) = 94.3 / 87.5 micro.
lookahead_frames: not_stated (inference uses T-frame units, T=12, and each unit's score comes from the frame with the largest MSE in the unit, so in the frame-level variant a frame can depend on up to 11 future frames; Eq. 11 min-max over the sequence uses whole-video statistics; the * object-level variant follows the SSMTL setup and is not detailed)
notes: CORRECTED: the supervision_evidence numbers for the ▽ rows were wrong ('93.8? / 87.5'). From Table 3 and the Sec. 4.4 text: Ours▽* (Three Tasks) = 94.3 Avenue / 87.5 ShT micro, and Ours▽ (frame-level, virtual data) = 93.2 / 86.2. The 93.8 is the Avenue macro of Ours* (Three Tasks). The class and flags are unchanged. * = multi-task backbone [11] = Georgescu et al. CVPR 2021 SSMTL, object-level with a detector ('we perform the proxy task at the object-level with the multi-task backbone [11]'). The reported numbers are therefore object-centric, and SSMTL itself is one-class. The plain I3D frame-level variant gives 92.4 / 85.1 (frame_centric), which matches the text's 85.1 ShT. Eq. 11 min-max normalises PSNR over t'=1..T 'following [20, 41, 46]' (Liu et al. 2018 style, i.e. per test video), so the normalisation uses test-time statistics including future frames. Whether the * variant scores with Eq. 11 or with SSMTL's scorer is not stated. No temporal smoothing is mentioned. One hyperparameter set (T=12, omega=0.5, w1=w2=w3=1); the T ablation was run on ShT/Campus. Micro and macro reported. No Ped2.

title: Self-Distilled Masked Auto-Encoders are Efficient Video Anomaly Detectors (AED-MAE)
authors: Ristea, Croitoru, Ionescu, Popescu, Khan, Shah
approach: Lightweight masked autoencoder (ViT) with self-distillation, motion-gradient weighting and synthetic-anomaly augmentation; frame-level
protocol_notes: Micro and macro reported. Training videos are augmented with synthetic anomalies (UBnormal action segments superimposed), so training is not purely on normal videos, though no real anomalies are used. Frame-level, no detector. FPS measured on GPU only.
hardware: one Nvidia GeForce 'GTX 3090' 24GB (as written in the paper)
supervision_evidence: arXiv 2306.12041 Sec. 4.1: 'To augment the normal training videos, we sample abnormal events from the UBnormal data set' and 'The probability of augmenting a frame from Avenue, ShanghaiTech or UCSD Ped2 is 0.25.' The anomaly map is added as an extra target channel and the classification head is trained on it (Sec. 3). The released configs set percent_abnormal=0.25.
lookahead_frames: Released code: input_3d=True in both configs, so the model input concatenates frames t-3, t and t+3 (data/test_dataset.py, direction=-3/+3), a 3-frame lookahead. The test-time motion-gradient map is |x(t-1) - x(t+1)| (extract_gradients.py, step=1 in the script's Avenue calls). On top of that comes a per-video temporal Gaussian (util/abnormal_utils.py filt, zero-padded np.correlate, kernel peak at offset -1): Avenue 37 taps, sigma 11, offsets -18..+18; ShT 899 taps, sigma 282, offsets -449..+449. Total lookahead is about 21 frames for Avenue and 452 for ShT.
notes: CORRECTED: the old lookahead said the model input was 'a single frame plus motion gradients from consecutive frames, with direction not stated'. The released code feeds frames t-3, t, t+3 (input_3d=True) and a central-difference gradient |x(t-1) - x(t+1)|, so the model itself sees future frames. Lookahead totals were updated. Added detail: main.py evaluates the test set every epoch and saves checkpoint-best.pth (teacher) and checkpoint-best-student.pth by best test micro AUC, and inference loads those, so checkpoints are selected on the test set. Unchanged: the paper only says 'apply another temporal Gaussian filter to smooth the values' plus 3D filtering of anomaly volumes, with no sigma. The code uses per-dataset filter range and sigma. ShanghaiTech gets per-video min-max normalisation after filtering (normalize_scores=True) while Avenue does not. The code's score is teacher + student-teacher discrepancy for Avenue (L2) and teacher only for ShT (L1), not the paper's alpha=0.4, beta=0.3, gamma=0.3 'for all data sets'. The patch size is per dataset (16/8/4). The released code covers only Avenue and ShT, so Ped2 post-processing is not public. Frame-level, no detector. Open-set style supervision through pasted UBnormal anomalies.

title: Lightning Fast Video Anomaly Detection via Adversarial Knowledge Distillation
authors: Croitoru, Ristea, Dascalescu, Ionescu, Khan, Shah
venue: Computer Vision and Image Understanding (2024), DOI 10.1016/j.cviu.2024.104074
approach: Knowledge distillation: lightweight student distilled (multi-scale adversarial) from object-centric teachers; detector-free at test time
protocol_notes: Micro and macro. Teachers detect objects with a pre-trained YOLOv3, used only during training. A good accuracy-speed reference for edge deployment.
hardware: Nvidia GeForce 'GTX 3090' 24GB; CPU-only Intel i9 3.7GHz gives 88 FPS
supervision_evidence: arXiv 2211.15597 Sec. 4.2: the student replicates the outputs of teachers 'Georgescu et al., 2022b, 2021'; 'We use the official code to train the teachers.' Sec. 2: 'Georgescu et al. (2022b) extended the framework by introducing pseudo-anomalies during training and attaching classifiers to discriminate between normal and pseudo-abnormal samples.' The student itself is trained on normal training frames with teacher anomaly maps as targets (config: av_train_labels_path_teacher1/2).
lookahead_frames: 3 frames from the input triplet (t-3, t, t+3; data/shanghai_dataset.py and avenue_dataset.py read direction=-3 and +3). The released code adds a per-video temporal Gaussian (utils/stats_manager.py filt: 301 taps, sigma 21, zero-padded np.correlate, offsets -150..+150, peak at -1). Total is about 153 future frames.
notes: CONFIRMED. The pseudo-anomaly supervision is indirect, inherited through the BA-AED teacher (T1). Counting only the student's own training, it would be one-class; T2 = SSMTL is one-class. The teachers use YOLOv3 objects during training only; the student is detector-free and frame-level at test time. Temporal score smoothing is not mentioned in the paper; the paper's Gaussian blur is spatial, on the teacher maps. The released evaluator applies a fixed-sigma Gaussian per video with no min-max normalisation, and computes both micro and macro AUC. Added detail: trainer.py runs eval_net on the test loader every epoch and saves best_model.pkl by the best test micro AUC of the MIX head, so checkpoints are selected on the test set. Per-dataset output-head resolutions: 1/4/16 for Avenue and ShT, 1/30/60 for Ped2.

title: Feature Prediction Diffusion Model for Video Anomaly Detection (FPDM)
approach: Diffusion (DDIM) predicting frame features with prediction + refinement modules; image features, no detector
protocol_notes: One-class. DDIM sampling at t=0.25T gives a '20× speed-up compared with DDPM', but no FPS is given. No Ped2.
hardware: not stated in text read
supervision_evidence: ICCV 2023 paper: 'our method belongs to the one-class type'; Table 1 'AUC of different one-class VAD methods'. The method aims 'to learn the distribution of normal samples'. Two DDIM modules (prediction + refinement) are trained on the training videos, and the Avenue 'training split contains only normal samples'. UCF-Crime video-level labels are 'discarded' in the one-class setting.
lookahead_frames: 0 in the model ('four consecutive neighbor frames to predict the fifth', following Liu et al. future-frame prediction; Score = MSE between the refined and original features of the k-th frame, Eq. 10). Any score post-processing is not stated.
notes: CONFIRMED. Frame-level 32x32x4 latent features from a pre-trained 'slight encoder' with unsupervised pretraining; no detector. Added detail: the paper cites the encoder as [48], which in its reference list is CLIP (Radford et al.). The description (4-channel latent, matching frozen decoder used for visualisation) fits the LDM autoencoder [49] (Rombach et al.), so the citation is probably off by one. No score smoothing or normalisation is mentioned. One hyperparameter set is reported for all datasets (60 epochs incl. 12 warm-up, T=1k, lr 1e-5, 200-step DDIM schedule, t=0.25T taken from [28, 63]). The code link in the PDF ('available at FPDM') could not be recovered from the text layer. No Ped2. Uses the standard one-class ShT split (330 train videos).

title: Normalizing Flows for Human Pose Anomaly Detection (STG-NF)
approach: Pose density: spatio-temporal graph normalizing flow on tracked skeletons
protocol_notes: AlphaPose + YOLOX detector + PoseFlow tracking. The 189 FPS appears to cover the flow model only; the paper notes that the 83M-param pose estimator and tracker are separate preprocessing. Human-only. No Avenue/Ped2 in the paper; re-runs by others report Avenue about 60-62 (AccI-VAD Table 2: 60.1; VideoPatchCore Table 1: 61.8), so it fails on non-human anomalies.
hardware: single NVIDIA Titan Xp
supervision_evidence: Sec. 4: 'The first setting is the common unsupervised anomaly detection setting, where the training data consists of only normal videos ... We evaluate the ShanghaiTech Campus dataset [23] on the unsupervised setting'. The supervised variant (priors N(10,I)/N(-10,I) with abnormal training samples, Sec. 4.1 'Training') is used only on UBnormal.
lookahead_frames: 11 frames from the 24-frame segment (official scoring_utils.py writes each segment score at start+seg_len/2; metadata[3] is the segment start), plus much more from the non-causal Gaussian smoothing (6 stacked gaussian_filter1d passes with sigma 1..6, about 9.5 frames effective sigma)
notes: CONFIRMED. Paper Sec. 4: the ShT 85.9 is the standard one-class split, reported as frame AUC 'sometimes called Micro AUC'. It is not the weakly supervised split. The paper never mentions temporal smoothing. Official smooth_scores applies gaussian_filter1d per test clip for sig in range(1,7), which is non-causal. No per-video score normalisation: clips are concatenated and only +/-inf (frames with no person) are clamped to the global max/min. The per-segment pose normalisation (zero mean, unit std) is input normalisation inside the segment, not score normalisation. Per-dataset setting: segment window tau=24 for ShT and 16 for UBnormal (Sec. 4.1), with a tau ablation in the supplement. The frame score is the minimum pose log-likelihood over the people in the frame. The pose pipeline (AlphaPose + YOLOX + PoseFlow) is off-the-shelf.

title: Hierarchical Semantic Contrast for Scene-aware Video Anomaly Detection (HSC)
approach: Object-centric scene-aware contrastive learning (ViT appearance, HRNet skeleton, PoseConv3D motion, DeepLabV3+ scene) with motion augmentation
protocol_notes: Micro AUC. The Avenue/ShT fields use the motion-augmentation variant, which 'generate[s] both normal and abnormal samples' (pseudo-anomalies). The base model gives 92.4 / 83.0. Ped2 uses only the scene-appearance stream (†). YOLOv3 + FairMOT. Heavy multi-model pipeline.
hardware: not stated
supervision_evidence: Sec. 3.5: augmented skeleton samples 'are not guaranteed to be normal', so the trained model splits them by reconstruction error, and 'we leverage both normal and abnormal samples to additionally train a binary classifier on the motion stream using a cross-entropy loss'. At test time the motion-stream score is 'replaced by the anomaly probability output by the binary classifier'. Table 2/4: MA row = 93.7 Avenue / 83.4 ShT, which are the listed values.
lookahead_frames: up to 15 frames from the 16-frame clip (official get_frame_scores assigns the clip max to all 16 frames), plus a centred Gaussian (code: gaussian_filter(np.arange(1, gaussian_len), sigma), i.e. 77 taps/sigma 30 on ShT, 69/15 on Avenue, 59/6 on Ped2, so about 29-38 more future frames)
notes: CONFIRMED. The pseudo-anomalies are generated from target normal skeletons only (no external data), but they are explicitly labelled abnormal and train a classifier whose output is the score, so the class holds. The base HSC without motion augmentation is one-class: 92.4 Avenue / 83.0 ShT (Table 2/4). Ped2 98.1 (dagger) uses only the scene-appearance stream, which is one-class. Paper: 'we apply a Gaussian filter for temporal smoothing over all video clips'. Official HSC_testing.py applies a global min-max over the concatenated test set (not per video) and np.correlate over the concatenated sequence, so smoothing crosses video boundaries. In the released code the MA path only loads precomputed motion scores from a .npy file (augmentMotion is false in all released yamls), so the 93.7/83.4 cannot be reproduced from the released testing code alone. Per-dataset settings: Gaussian length/sigma, num_cluster (1/2/23), batch size (paper 128 Ped2/Avenue and 512 ShT; the yamls say 128/256/256), and the stream set on Ped2 (removeMotionBranch). Pretrained YOLOv3, FairMOT, ViT, HRNet, PoseConv3D and DeepLabV3+ are used. Micro AUC. Consistency flag for the table: HSC and FastAno are put in this class because the authors generate samples they explicitly call abnormal from target normal data. SSMTL's frame-skip task does something functionally similar but is kept one-class (see rows 32/34).

title: Diversity-Measurable Anomaly Detection (DMAD)
approach: Reconstruction/memory: pyramid deformation module measuring anomaly diversity on a VQ memory AE (frame-level)
protocol_notes: Micro AUC (all frames pooled). The repo README says the pre-processing files, 'e.g. background template for ShanghaiTech', must be downloaded separately. Ties MULDE on Ped2 (99.7).
hardware: not stated
supervision_evidence: Sec. 3.1: autoencoder methods 'model normal data distribution by minimizing the following reconstruction loss'. Sec. 2: 'models trained with only normal data cannot reconstruct anomalies'. The contaminated-training experiment (Sec. 4.6, abnormal events mixed into Ped2 training) is a separate ablation, not the headline numbers.
lookahead_frames: 0 for the model (4 past frames predict the next). The official post-processing adds lookahead. Ped2: one centred 11-frame robust moving average (5 future frames). Avenue (process_avenue.py): two 11-frame passes (about 10 future). ShT: a per-video 69-frame conf_avg (33 future), then two 55-frame passes over the concatenated test set (26 future each), so about 85 future frames, followed by a causal Kalman filter.
notes: CORRECTED (lookahead only; class and flags unchanged). The previous row said 'stacked 55-frame windows (about 27 future)' for ShT. Evaluate_shanghai.py first runs conf_avg with the utils default size=69 ('robust+') per video, then conf_avg(...,55,'average') on the concatenated list, then conf_avg(comb,55), then the Kalman filter(). On Avenue, process_avenue.py applies the 11-frame conf_avg twice. Further code facts. (1) Per-video min-max (anomaly_score_list_inv) is used on Ped2 and ShT. The final Avenue AUC comes from process_avenue.py, which uses a global min-max over the whole test set. (2) Code quirk: utils.conf_avg initialises its output with ones, so on ShT the first 35 and last 33 frames of every test video get score 1 (max anomaly) before the later passes. The Ped2 version inserts 1 for the first 5 frames. (3) The code fuses three error terms with fixed weights [0.2, 0.4, 0.6] on all datasets, while the paper states a single alpha=0.2. (4) process_avenue.py and utils.auc3_mp/auc4_mp contain a weight grid search that maximises AUC against the test labels. It is disabled by default (search_step=1), so the reported numbers are not proven test-tuned, but the tooling exists. The paper mentions only an 'average kernel' for videos, which is spatial (k* in Eq. 22). Dataset-specific steps: frame-difference removal of static anomalies on Avenue only; mask-based anomaly-map normalisation on ShT only; per-dataset models; epochs 60/60/10. The ShT model also receives a scene/view index (vidx). Micro AUC ('all frames together').

title: EVAL: Explainable Video Anomaly Localization
approach: Interpretable exemplar-based: high-level appearance attributes + motion features, scene-specific exemplar nearest neighbours
protocol_notes: Optimised for localisation (RBDC/TBDC), not frame AUC. Ped1/Ped2 are used for parameter tuning, so there is no Ped2 frame AUC. FPS statements are inconsistent: Table 8 gives Ped2 32, Avenue 112, Street Scene 12 fps; the main text says '20 to 100 fps'; the appendix says Avenue 'over 6 frames/sec' and Ped2 under 1 frame/sec. fps is therefore left null.
hardware: NVIDIA Quadro RTX 8000 (features) + Intel Xeon E5-2680 v4 CPU (NN search)
supervision_evidence: Sec. 3: 'The high-level attribute learning stage is done only once and uses training samples that are independent of any video anomaly detection dataset' and 'Our outside data is not used to build models of a scene'. Sec. 1: 'there is no training of deep networks for each new environment'. Sec. 3.2: greedy exemplar selection (threshold th) on nominal video per spatial region.
lookahead_frames: up to 9 frames: t=10-frame video volumes with temporal stride t (non-overlapping in time); each volume's score is assigned to every pixel of all its frames
notes: CONFIRMED. Training-free in the memory-bank sense. The appearance and motion attribute CNNs are trained once on external data (CIFAR-10/100, MIO-TCD, self-collected webcam videos with TV-L1 pseudo ground truth). The target normal training videos are used only to build region-wise nearest-neighbour exemplar sets (non-parametric). The distance normalisation constants Z are computed once on Ped1/Ped2. Exemplar threshold th=1.5 is chosen on Ped1/Ped2 with modified ground truth and fixed for all datasets. Region size is set per dataset by a rule (about one person's height): 32/128/100 px for Ped2/Avenue/ShT. That is a per-dataset setting, but not tuned on test. The frame score is not written explicitly; it is derived from the pixel-wise max anomaly map. No smoothing is stated. The paper reports no Ped2 frame AUC (Ped2 is used for tuning). The method targets RBDC/TBDC; frame AUC is reported 'for completeness'. AUC aggregation is not labelled.

title: SSMTL++: Revisiting Self-Supervised Multi-Task Learning for Video Anomaly Detection
venue: Computer Vision and Image Understanding (2023) (arXiv comment 'Accepted in Computer Vision and Image Understanding')
approach: Object-centric self-supervised multi-task learning (9 proxy tasks) with transformer/SSPCAB heads
protocol_notes: The best Avenue (v1) and best ShT (v2) numbers come from different variants. YOLOv3 + SelFlow optical flow; the paper names optical flow as the main speed bottleneck. No Ped2.
hardware: single GeForce 'GTX 3090' 24GB
supervision_evidence: Sec. 3.3, T5: the shared encoder is trained by gradient ascent to reproduce images 'from an out-of-distribution data set ... containing flowers ..., textures ..., and ImageNet ... classes that do not appear in urban surveillance videos'. Sec. 4.3.4: SSMTL++v1 = T1, T2, T3, T5; SSMTL++v2 = T1, T2, T3, T6 (no T5). Avenue 93.7 = v1 (Table 7).
lookahead_frames: 3 frames from the object sequence (length 7, i-3..i+3, centred on frame i), plus a 3D mean filter and a temporal Gaussian filter (sigma not stated)
notes: CONFIRMED (flags unchanged; per_dataset_tuning now has a stronger reason). The class differs per field. Avenue 93.7 = SSMTL++v1, which uses external OOD pseudo-anomalies (T5). ShT 83.8 (Table 8 micro) = SSMTL++v2, which uses only target normal data plus self-supervised T1/T2/T3/T6, effectively one-class. Stronger reason for per_dataset_tuning=yes: Sec. 4.2/4.3 says 'To draw our conclusions after each preliminary experiment, we only look at the ... micro AUC', and all preliminary choices were made on the Avenue TEST set (Tables 1-6, Fig. 3). That covers detector choice, backbone, task combinations, and the epoch at which pseudo-anomalies are introduced. Those choices were then transferred to ShT/UBnormal. In addition, the list's best numbers mix variants by dataset. Otherwise SSMTL's hyperparameters are kept, with a 15% training-video validation split for checkpoint choice. Paper Sec. 3.4: 3D mean filter, frame score = max, then 'we apply a temporal Gaussian filter to smooth the frame-level predictions'. Detections: YOLOv3 (conf 0.8) + SelFlow optical-flow objects. Micro and macro AUC are both reported; the listed values are micro. UBnormal is trained on normal videos only.

title: FastAno: Fast Anomaly Detection via Spatio-temporal Patch Transformation
